_readme: daemons[0] is the factory clock: dotpi's `pacemaker serve --every 60` (see `pacemaker serve --help`).
init starts it once per boot and never restarts it (rip-cage-vpxk tracks a restart policy).
Every tick reads the seat roster through herdr, so serve needs HERDR_SOCKET_PATH, herdr's own env var.
The start command reads it at runtime from the cage's composed boot descriptor (whichever multiplexer
start sets it) rather than naming another recipe's path (ADR-027 D4). None found: it warns and runs anyway.
health asks the clock itself: `pacemaker status` reports arm.armed=true while serve holds its pidfile lock.

daemons.name: dotpi-pacemaker
daemons.start: _rc_sock=$(jq -r '.multiplexers[]?.start // empty' "${RC_BOOT_DESCRIPTOR:-/etc/rip-cage/boot.json}" 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/.*HERDR_SOCKET_PATH=\([^; ]*\).*/\1/p' | head -n 1); if [ -n "$_rc_sock" ]; then export HERDR_SOCKET_PATH="$_rc_sock"; else echo '[rip-cage] WARNING: no HERDR_SOCKET_PATH in the composed boot descriptor; pacemaker ticks will record server_not_running until one exists' >&2; fi; exec pacemaker serve --every 60
